error_message: Per-row 🖨️ button in child table grid is visible but not clickable in inline (non-popup) mode
root_cause: frappe.ui.form.on(childDoctype, "fieldname", fn) only fires through the child form script_manager, which is only active when the row is open as a popup dialog. The static inline grid renders the button element but clicking it never reaches that handler.
fix: Added jQuery delegation via grid.wrapper.on("click.ee_print", "[data-fieldname=ee_print_label]", fn) in bindGridPrintClick(). Delegation fires at the DOM level regardless of Frappe form state, catching clicks in both inline and popup modes. Popup mode also retains frappe.ui.form.on handler (no conflict as popup dialog is outside grid wrapper DOM).

error_message: NameError: name 'TEST' is not defined inside patched frappe.sendmail when running test script via exec(open(...).read()) in bench console
root_cause: bench console (IPython) runs exec() with separate globals/locals dicts. Module-level assignments land in locals, but nested function __globals__ points at the globals dict, so free variables (TEST, real_sendmail) referenced inside the callback are not found.
fix: Avoid free globals in callbacks run via exec: bind values as default arguments, e.g. def patched_sendmail(*a, _test='x', _real=frappe.sendmail, **k). Also feed multi-line scripts via exec(open(path).read()) rather than piping raw blank-line-containing heredocs into the REPL.

error_message: Cumulative reorder email lists items that are already well-stocked (e.g. مزيل صدأ صيني وسط: 24 on hand vs reorder level 1; كلاكس جنير: 5 vs 1).
root_cause: Email filtered open auto-reorder MRs by received_qty < qty. But this shop restocks via Stock Reconciliation / Stock Count, never via Purchase Receipt, so auto-reorder MRs never get received_qty filled and stay status=Pending forever. received_qty < qty is therefore permanently true even after the shelf is refilled, so restocked items keep showing. Also produced duplicate rows (one MR per day the item was short).
fix: Gate the cumulative query on LIVE stock instead of MR receipt: JOIN tabBin (on item+warehouse) and tabItem Reorder (parent+warehouse), keep only rows where COALESCE(actual_qty,0) <= warehouse_reorder_level. Dedupe to one row per item+warehouse via ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item_code,warehouse ORDER BY transaction_date DESC, name DESC) and WHERE rn=1. Template now shows on_hand / reorder_level / reorder_qty instead of qty / remaining_qty. Verified: 139 line rows -> 41 genuinely-short items; the two reported items excluded.

error_message: User: the reorder ('material') email sent to mohamedelsayedbaba@gmail.com at the 00:00 scheduled run is corrupted/empty. Decoded subject was ERPNext's DEFAULT 'طلبات الشراء التلقائية - تم الإنشاء' (Auto Material Requests Generated), with no PDF attachment and the bare default reorder_item.html body.
root_cause: easy_entry/__init__.py monkeypatches erpnext.stock.reorder_item.send_email_notification with the Arabic+PDF override. The patch only applies when the current easy_entry package is (re)imported. The supervisor-managed scheduler+worker processes (group frappe-bench-workers) were started ~June 10 and held a STALE in-memory copy of the easy_entry modules from before the override code was finalized (override file last edited June 13, still uncommitted on disk). Long-lived RQ workers do not re-import changed .py files, so the 00:00 job ran ERPNext's unpatched default send_email_notification. Verified: in a FRESH process, importing easy_entry correctly repoints the function and the override yields subject 'أصناف تحتاج إعادة طلب (43)' with a 48KB PDF.
fix: Operational, not code: restart the worker+scheduler so they re-import current code -> `sudo supervisorctl restart frappe-bench-workers:` (or `bench restart`). After ANY Python change under easy_entry/, workers MUST be restarted or scheduled jobs keep running the old code. Immediate user request handled by re-rendering + resending the corrected email (PDF previewed via wkhtmltoimage first) to the test inbox with now=True. NOTE: the supervisorctl restart was blocked by the Claude permission classifier as out-of-scope; user must run it (or grant permission) for future 00:00 runs to use the override.

error_message: Barcode scan in Item Manager does not find items by barcode; no camera scanner button
root_cause: get_items() only searched i.name and i.item_name — never joined tabItem Barcode. BarcodeScanner.vue was not imported/used in ItemManager.vue at all.
fix: Added LEFT JOIN tabItem Barcode bc in _ITEMS_FROM, added bc.barcode LIKE to search condition, added GROUP BY i.name and COUNT(DISTINCT i.name) for count query. Added BarcodeScanner import + showScanner ref + onCameraScanned + camera icon button next to search input. PLUS: gunicorn master (--preload) was not restarted after Python change — sent SIGTERM to PID 997 so supervisor restarted it with fresh code. kill -HUP only restarts workers, not the master; code stays stale. Need kill -TERM or bench restart to pick up Python changes.

error_message: User reported the '38 * 25' item label print format's barcode is bordered/gapped on the left side.
root_cause: code128_svg() built the SVG viewBox as '0 0 total_w 100' (module-unit width x fixed height 100), which does not match the physical output aspect ratio (width_mm:height_mm, e.g. 36:11). preserveAspectRatio="none" is meant to force non-uniform stretch to fill exactly, but is not reliably honored across renderers when the caller also relies on smart-shrinking-affected CSS mm units. Actual root confirmation: raw wkhtmltopdf (without Frappe's disable-smart-shrinking flag) distorts mm-based CSS layouts non-uniformly ('smart shrinking' makes the pixel/dpi ratio non-constant per wkhtmltopdf --extended-help); the true production path (frappe.utils.pdf.get_pdf) already applies disable-smart-shrinking for wkhtmltopdf > 0.12.3, but the SVG's own viewBox/physical-size aspect mismatch was a separate, compounding defect that a mismatched-aspect-ratio viewBox made worse under any imperfect preserveAspectRatio handling.
fix: Rewrote code128_svg() to compute bar x/width directly in mm (scale = width_mm / total_w) and set viewBox="0 0 {width_mm} {height_mm}" so the viewBox aspect ratio exactly equals the physical width_mm:height_mm ratio — eliminating any dependency on preserveAspectRatio or CSS width:100% being honored correctly. Verified by rendering both '38 * 25' and '50 * 25' formats through wkhtmltopdf with the exact flags Frappe's get_pdf() uses (--disable-smart-shrinking --disable-javascript --disable-local-file-access) and confirming near-symmetric quiet zones via PIL pixel measurement (~4.1mm vs ~4.3mm, previously ~10.8mm vs ~0.1mm). Live-confirmed after restarting frappe-bench-web: fetched a real PDF from the production /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_pdf endpoint and rasterized it — barcode renders symmetric. User also confirmed via a photo of a freshly printed physical label (Xprinter thermal printer) showing even margins on both sides, replacing the earlier photo that showed the barcode flush against the right edge.

error_message: Cash loans given via POS (sold as a 'سلف نقدية' item) were counted as full Gross Profit on reports like Gross Profit Simple, even though the shop always expects the same amount back.
root_cause: The original implementation modeled a cash loan as a Sales Invoice line for a special item, then tried to patch over the profit distortion with a Sales Invoice.validate hook forcing incoming_rate = rate. That only zeroed the per-line profit calc after the fact -- the amount still ran through Sales Invoice Item, so any report reading that table (or a different profit formula) could still show it as revenue. It also required creating a fake Item/Item Group for something that is not a sale at all.
fix: Deleted cash_loan_items.py and its Sales Invoice validate hook. Replaced with a dedicated Cash Loan doctype + easy_entry/api/cash_loan.py that posts a plain Journal Entry (Dr/Cr 'Cash Loans Receivable' vs the Mode of Payment account) -- no Sales Invoice or Item involved, so it is structurally invisible to sales/GP reports rather than patched to look zero.
